clue.text: It's serious for woman (and two unfortunate men!)

definitions.text: It's serious for woman (and two unfortunate men!)

parts.words: It's serious for woman (and two unfortunate men!)
parts.note: a grave offence for a wife who has taken two husbands at once, both of them unlucky to be sharing her

explanation.surface: A grim warning about something serious for a woman and two hapless men.
explanation.definitionFit: Being married to two spouses at the same time is a crime, so it is serious for the woman and unfortunate for both husbands.

clue.text: Boastful quality, nice one written around poster

indicators.note: written around says the praise is set down round the poster

parts.note: bravo is a cry of 'nice one'
an ad, advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: Someone scrawls 'nice one' round a poster in a show of swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a boastful show of courage, a swaggering quality.

clue.text: Audibly, escort ridiculed

indicators.note: audibly says the word is to be spoken out loud

parts.note: to guide is to escort

explanation.surface: An escort is mocked out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to make fun of them, so guyed means ridiculed.

clue.text: See 23
Fearful of something hot appearing in photo

indicators.note: appearing in says one piece sits inside the word for photo

parts.note: a pic is a photo
a hob is a cooker top, something hot

explanation.surface: Someone is scared of a hot thing showing up in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a phobia is irrationally afraid, so phobic is an adjective meaning fearful.

clue.text: Hex and its heading with nine semicircles?

parts.note: its heading is the first letter of hex
letter shapes holding nine half circles: four Os, each two half circles, with a D, one half circle

explanation.surface: A curse is drawn as its first letter with nine half-circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Shapes: O is a full circle, two semicircles; D is one semicircle on a stick. OODOO holds nine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx or curse, the same as a hex.

clue.text: Successful time, say, managed to get in to make a comeback

parts.note: a boom is a successful period

indicators.note: to get in says one piece enters the other

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
ran means managed

explanation.surface: A good spell, say, was run so well that it led to a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: To boomerang is to return to where it started, like the throwing stick, so to make a comeback.

clue.text: Vital energy brought to hole is wind

parts.note: chi is the vital energy of Chinese thought
a nook is a small hole or corner

explanation.surface: Life force fed into a hole is just hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinook is a warm dry wind down the eastern Rockies.

clue.text: Extra ten twists occupying Archer, the contortionist?

indicators.note: occupying says the scrambled letters sit inside the name

parts.note: Mary Archer, wife of the novelist Jeffrey Archer, made bendy: a supple Mary

indicators.note: twists means the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An extra ten contortions fill the act of Archer the contortionist.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer is Mary Archer, a British scientist and wife of the novelist Jeffrey Archer; 'twists' makes ENT, which lands inside her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary means additional, extra.

clue.text: 3's introduction to ballads playable — we thank arrangement

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of ballads
an arrangement of letters reorders them, as a musical arrangement reworks a tune

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Mancini introduces some playable ballads and the musicians thank him for the arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is MANCINI, so '3's' means a Mancini piece. 'arrangement' shuffles PLAYABLE WE THANK into ABY ELEPHANT WALK, after B from ballads.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby Elephant Walk is a famous instrumental by Henry Mancini, so it is one of the composer's pieces.

clue.text: Disgraced leader about to regret backing possible cause of paralysis?

indicators.note: backing says the whole assembly is read in the reverse direction
about says the leader's name goes round the other words

parts.note: Richard Nixon, the US president who resigned in disgrace
taken as written
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician returns to express regret over something that might paralyse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgraced leader' is Richard Nixon, who resigned the US presidency; 'about' and 'backing' together give NIXOTORUEN read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve poison attacks the nervous system and can cause paralysis, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Indian leader coming after two close predecessors?

definitions.text: Indian leader coming after two close predecessors?

indicators.note: coming after says the leader letter is placed behind the predecessors

parts.note: the two letters just before I in the alphabet are G and H, read here as the phrase G AND H

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Indian

explanation.surface: An Indian politician follows two of his near forerunners into office.
explanation.walkthrough: I, the leader of 'Indian', comes straight after G and H in the alphabet, which are its close predecessors; spelt as G AND H plus I, the whole clue also describes the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement, and Indira and Rajiv Gandhi were later prime ministers.

clue.text: Polish born amid disease in enclosed space

indicators.note: amid says these pieces sit in the middle of the disease

parts.note: pox is a disease
to hone is to polish or sharpen

explanation.surface: A Pole born during an outbreak of illness finds himself shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' wants to be the nationality; it is the verb, to hone.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone kiosk is a small enclosed space with a door, so it is a fair if loose description.

clue.text: 23 3's cast-iron introduction to one proposing

indicators.note: introduction to here means being introduced into, put inside the proposer

parts.note: a mover is one who proposes a motion

indicators.note: cast metal is poured and reshaped, so these letters are remoulded

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Henry Mancini makes a tough opening statement to someone putting forward a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 3 is HENRY MANCINI, so '23 3's' means one of his pieces; 'cast' makes ONRI. 'cast-iron' looks like one adjective, meaning solid, but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Moon River, from Breakfast at Tiffany's, is Henry Mancini's best-known song.

clue.text: Person going up quietly in lift sees personalised sign

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a man is a person

indicators.note: in says the quiet letter goes inside the lift

parts.note: to elate is to lift the spirits
p is the musical notation for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone rising quietly in an elevator spots a sign with their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate bears a person's name on a door or desk, a sign personalised to them.

clue.text: See 9
Possible cause of your headache needing doctor's note

parts.note: ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is a fatigue illness that can bring headaches
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: Something giving you a headache calls for a doctor's note.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note, usually within an office.

clue.text: 23 3's in need of a wash with both hands immersed

indicators.note: immersed says the hands are dipped inside the dirty word

parts.note: mucky means dirty, in need of a wash
R and L stand for right and left hands

explanation.surface: Henry Mancini is filthy and plunges both hands in to wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 3 is HENRY MANCINI, whose theme for the TV series Mr Lucky is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Lucky was a TV series whose theme music was written by Henry Mancini.

clue.text: 23 3's writer carrying tune composed around Scott Joplin's hollow work?

indicators.note: carrying says the writer holds the rest within it

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool, a writer

indicators.note: around says the reworked tune goes round the emptied work
composed means put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: hollow says the inside letter is taken out

parts.note: a rag, ragtime piece, is Scott Joplin's typical work

explanation.surface: A writer hums a tune built round one of Scott Joplin's ragtime pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Scott Joplin was the American ragtime composer, so his typical work is a rag; 'hollow' empties it, and 'composed' makes TEUN, which goes round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Gunn is the TV detective series whose theme tune Henry Mancini wrote.

clue.text: Bird protected by another without beginning and without end

indicators.note: protected by says the bird sits inside the other bird
without beginning says the first letter is removed

parts.note: another bird: teal, a duck
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: One bird shelters inside another, with no start and no finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without beginning and without end' tempts as one definition; only 'without end' is, while 'without beginning' trims TEAL to EAL to hold TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, lasting without end.

clue.text: Nice one to come up with 20 type of energy

indicators.note: to come up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: in Nice, in France, one is un
the answer to 20, patent, means obvious, and so does clear

explanation.surface: A Nice one turns up with a patent for a new kind of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so 'one' is UN, reversed to NU.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear energy is a type of energy from atomic nuclei.

clue.text: Obvious case, one dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed says one piece is sent out of the word

parts.note: a patient is a medical case
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An obvious legal case where one party is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means plain and obvious, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: See 9
Set about containing spasm as moral code

indicators.note: containing says the scrambled word holds the spasm
about means around in a jumble, so the letters of set are reordered

parts.note: anagram fodder
hic is the spasm of a hiccup

explanation.surface: A set of people gather round a spasm and decide it is a moral question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes ETS; 'Set' looks like a verb but is the anagram fodder, and HIC is the sound of a hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the principles of right conduct, a moral code.

clue.text: Composer in nice harmony, not the Ring Cycle

indicators.note: a cycle turns round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

indicators.note: not the says the ring shape is removed

parts.note: anagram fodder
a ring is O-shaped, the letter O

explanation.surface: A composer works in nice harmony but steers clear of Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the Ring' removes O from IN NICE HARMONY, and 'Cycle' rearranges the rest; Ring Cycle suggests Wagner as a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Mancini was an American composer of film and television music.

clue.text: Figure another code out, thought not entirely

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
not entirely says one letter, the last, is cut from the words

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone works out a second cipher but only partly cracks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final E of ANOTHER CODE, and 'out' rearranges the rest; 'thought' reads as 'though', almost certainly a typing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: An octahedron is an eight-faced solid, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Season with dash of rocambole once turned over

indicators.note: turned over says the hidden letters are read backwards
a dash of something is a small amount, so only a few letters inside the words are taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook seasons a dish with a dash of rocambole, a garlic, flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Season with dash' as the definition and gave the hidden letters no signal; 'with dash of' is the signal, and 'Season' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is Christmas, the festive season.

clue.text: French girl's shape of catapult checked, unfinished

parts.note: a catapult is Y-shaped

indicators.note: unfinished says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: vetted means checked

explanation.surface: A French girl's catapult is inspected but the job is left half done.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvette is a French girl's name.

clue.text: Actor making sound of peahen?

indicators.note: making sound of says the words are spoken out loud

parts.note: a peahen is a pea-layer, since a hen is a layer, which said out loud gives the answer

explanation.surface: An actor imitates the cry of a female peacock.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is one who plays parts on stage, an actor.
